To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal chemistry of zirconates, silicates, and germanates is a very diverse and complex field, which has been investigated for over a century.

the zirconosilicate structures and their analogs can be divided into 41 topological structural groups, which differ in the composition of the polyhedral microensembles (PME) and coordination sequences [N(M)] and [N(T)], and that the topological groups are characterized by a set of invariant parameters, such as the PME composition and the number of vertices of the MT(6) framework.
The crystal structures of zircono-silicates and their synthetic analogs were classified into 41 topological MT-framework types based on the concept polyhedral micro-ensemble".
In summary, our research is concerned with

the first attempt to develop a method for topological classification of crystal structures based on the concept and methodology of PME and the first application of this method to the crystal chemistry of zirconolite and its analogs.
the development of the methodology for the analysis of the crystal structure of complex minerals and the description of their topological organization.
a new approach to the structural analysis of zirconosilosilicates and their structural analogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zirconosilicate and their analog structures can be classified by topological types and suprapolyhedra invariants.
the topological classification of zirconosils and their analogs is possible and that the topological types of the MT frameworks are the suprapolyhederal invariants.

the structural diversity of zirconosils and their analogs is determined by the variety of possible combinations of topologically different polyhedral microensembles (PME) and the number of their connections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method proposed is a powerful and universal tool for the analysis of MT-frameworks in crystal structures.
the structural diversity of MT frameworks in zirconosilicate structures can be classified by topological types of PME.

a new method of analysis and hierarchical classification of MT frameworks is developed, which can be applied for the description of the crystal chemistry of a wide variety of minerals, synthetic materials, and other materials with mixed frameworks of MO(6) and TO(4).
The main takeaway from our work is that

topological types of MT-frameworks can be considered as suprapolyhederals, i.e. as the highest invariant of the structure, which is independent of the choice of the crystal structure description method (TOPOS or other).
the topological classification is a powerful tool for analysis and classification of complex crystal structures.

the topological analysis of crystal structures of complex compounds with MT(6) composition is a promising tool for the classification of their structural types and for the prediction of new structures.
